West bedchamber built in parts/room-6.mjs: white bed head to the west wall (6,7,15) with a white carpet before it, a fence-and-slab bedside table with candles, a chest in the south-east corner under an east-wall shelf of top slabs holding candles and a potted poppy, and a standing lantern on the floor.
`$MCD room` says OK: 14 of 17 standable cells reached, min light 8, 0 dark cells. make.sh is green with 13 blocks placed, no REFUSED or off-palette, and the structure check is clean for this room.
The room view (room.png) reads as a bedroom: bed as focal piece, lane kept clear from the doorway at (8,14).
left: The shelf-top cells (10,10,14..16) are listed by the walk tool as unreached. They are standing spots on top of the east shelf, not floor, and the room verdict is OK, so this is only a note.
structure check flags dark_oak_slab at (10,9,17) as an orphan. That cell is on the main back wall, outside this part (shell or frame), so it is not mine to fix.
Not checked by eye at a player's height from inside the room. The check and the cutaway view were the only looks.
plan.md and elements.md have no checklist item for the room interiors, so nothing was ticked.

waste.what: Drew the room's furniture grid by hand in five layers, with the rows read as z (not x). I had the shelf slab on the wrong row, which left a candle floating; `$MCD check` found it, and a rebuild was needed.
waste.cost: 2 build cycles (1 bad layer row, 1 fix)
waste.tool: `mcd plan --only <room>` could print a per-layer grid labelled with the absolute (x,y,z) of each row and column, so the row/axis order is visible while drawing. A `layers` dry-run that prints the cell list it would write would also catch this before make.sh.

waste.what: Worked out the bed head and foot cells, the lane, and the light spots by hand (lantern on the floor for even light, since the room's ceiling is open and no block above can hang a lantern).
waste.cost: about 4 minutes of reasoning, no retries beyond the one above
waste.tool: `mcd room --suggest` already gives lantern spots; a furniture-placement helper that takes a focal cell and a wall and proposes a bed/chest/table layout with the lane kept clear would have saved the layout work.

companions.task: Confirm the bed's head and foot orientation and the white versus red choice against the concept, and check the carpet and bed sit square on the floor.
Review the light plan: a standing lantern for even light, the candles on the table and shelf, and whether the room needs a hanging lantern once the roof is in.
